== Problem ==
Buzz Bunny is hopping up and down a set of stairs, one step at a time. In how many ways can Buzz Bunny start on the ground, make a sequence of <imath>6</imath> hops, and end up back on the ground?
(For example, one sequence of hops is up-up-down-down-up-down.)

[[File:2024-AMC8-q13.png|center]]

<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ 4 \qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 5 \qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 6 \qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 8 \qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 12</imath>

==Solution 1==
Looking at the answer choices, you see that you can list them out. 
Doing this gets you:

<imath>\mathit{UUDDUD}</imath>

<imath>\mathit{UDUDUD}</imath>

<imath>\mathit{UUUDDD}</imath>

<imath>\mathit{UDUUDD}</imath>

<imath>\mathit{UUDUDD}</imath>

Counting all the paths listed above gets you <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B)} \ 5}</imath>.

~ALWAYSRIGHT11

==Solution 2 ==
Any combination can be written as some re-arrangement of <imath>\mathit{UUUDDD}</imath>. Clearly we must end going down, and start going up, so we need the number of ways to insert 2 <imath>U</imath>'s and 2 <imath>D</imath>'s into <imath>U\, \_ \, \_ \, \_ \, \_ \, D</imath>. There are <imath>{4\choose 2}=6</imath> ways, but we have to remove the case <imath>\mathit{UDDUUD}</imath>, giving us <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ 5}</imath>. 


- We know there are no more cases since there will be at least one <imath>U</imath> before we have a <imath>D</imath> (from the first <imath>U</imath>), at least two <imath>U</imath>'S before two <imath>D</imath>'s (since we removed the one case), and at least three <imath>U</imath>'s before three <imath>D</imath>'s, as we end with the third <imath>D</imath>. 

~Sahan Wijetunga

==Solution 3 (pretty good, but needs more explanation on the catalan numbers)==
These numbers are clearly the Catalan numbers. Since we have <imath>6</imath> steps, we need the third Catalan number, which is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ 5}</imath>.
~andliu766

with minor edits from ~shaopl2022

==Solution 4 (slightly confusing, but it was how i did it too)==
The first step must be a U, last step must be a D. After the third step we can get only position 3 or position 1. In the first case there is only one way: UUUDDD. In the second case we have two way to get this position UDU and UUD. Similarly, we have two way return to position 0 (UDD and DUD). Therefore, we have <imath>1 + 2 \cdot 2 = \boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ 5}</imath>.

with minor edits from ~shaopl2022

==Solution 5==
Realize that 2 of the solutions are <imath>\mathit{UDUDUD}</imath>, and <imath>\mathit{UUUDDD}</imath> which both consist of 3<imath>U</imath>’s and 3<imath>D</imath>’s. Then, there are five gaps where the <imath>U</imath>’s can go in the <imath>D</imath>’s so the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ 5}</imath>.

~OddPeppyBoots
